levels.title: Application and review-cycle identity
levels.objective: Resolve the exact drug, indication, formulation, application and review cycle before comparing evidence.
requirements: Bind application, indication, formulation and review cycle to primary regulatory records.
Keep delays, withdrawals, complete responses and approvals distinct; do not infer a decision from a target date.
completion_artifacts: Primary application/cycle identity record with unresolved aliases documented.

levels.title: Point-in-time evidence boundary
levels.objective: Separate the research cutoff, source availability, retrospective review and original prediction freeze.
requirements: Document the original prediction cutoff or explicitly preserve it as unknown.
Establish public availability before the research cutoff; an action date, printed date or folder year is insufficient.
Keep retrospective review timestamps separate from source publication and original prediction generation.
completion_artifacts: Timestamped source-availability ledger and explicit cutoff/freezing chronology.

levels.title: Source corpus and reconciliation
levels.objective: Collect and reconcile original documents, corrections and contradictory disclosures without promoting leads.
requirements: Retain original source bytes and hashes, accession identities and relevant locations.
Identify corrected, superseded, duplicated and unavailable documents and reconcile conflicting claims.
Exclude outcome-only and post-cutoff material from pre-decision findings.
completion_artifacts: Versioned source inventory, byte/hash provenance and exclusion/reconciliation log.

levels.title: Mechanistic and translational context
levels.objective: Assess biological rationale and translation to the proposed indication without assuming mechanism implies efficacy.
requirements: Document mechanism, target engagement, translational limitations and pathway-relevant evidence.
Distinguish direct clinical evidence from extrapolation across diseases, formulations or treatment settings.
completion_artifacts: Source-bound mechanistic rationale with contrary findings and translational limitations.

levels.title: Population and comparator suitability
levels.objective: Assess eligibility, selection and comparator relevance to the intended use.
requirements: Verify trial inclusion/exclusion, baseline characteristics and analysis-population denominators.
Justify concurrent comparator choice and identify selection or enrichment limitations.
completion_artifacts: Protocol-linked population/comparator assessment and denominator reconciliation.

levels.title: Design and protocol integrity
levels.objective: Evaluate randomization, blinding, amendments and deviations as potential sources of bias.
requirements: Review protocol versions, allocation methods, blinding, deviations and amendment timing.
Identify changes made after relevant data access and their consequences.
completion_artifacts: Dated protocol/amendment history and design-bias review.

levels.title: Power and prespecified analysis
levels.objective: Establish the power assumptions and statistical analysis plan frozen before relevant data review.
requirements: Verify sample-size assumptions, event targets and plausible treatment effects.
Retain the dated statistical plan and document changes relative to data access.
completion_artifacts: Prespecification and power assessment with dated protocol/SAP support.

levels.title: Primary efficacy and clinical meaning
levels.objective: Evaluate the primary treatment effect and uncertainty against clinically relevant thresholds.
requirements: Verify primary endpoint definition, analysis population, effect estimate, uncertainty and statistical assumptions.
Distinguish statistical significance, effect magnitude and clinical relevance.
completion_artifacts: Reproducible primary endpoint/effect-size assessment with uncertainty and clinical interpretation.

levels.title: Secondary endpoints and multiplicity
levels.objective: Evaluate secondary findings under the actual type-I-error strategy.
requirements: Reconstruct endpoint hierarchy, multiplicity control and failed gates.
Separate confirmatory secondary outcomes from nominal or exploratory findings.
completion_artifacts: Endpoint hierarchy and multiplicity assessment linked to prespecified tests.

levels.title: Estimands and missing data
levels.objective: Evaluate the treatment question, intercurrent events, exclusions and missing-data assumptions.
requirements: Reconcile randomized, treated, evaluable and reported analysis populations.
Assess estimand, intercurrent-event strategy, missingness assumptions and informative dropout.
completion_artifacts: Estimand/denominator reconciliation with missing-data bias assessment.

levels.title: Sensitivity, subgroup and durability
levels.objective: Challenge robustness across analyses, populations and time.
requirements: Review prespecified sensitivity analyses, subgroup interaction evidence and follow-up.
Separate within-arm change from between-arm effects and subgroup observations from proven heterogeneity.
completion_artifacts: Robustness assessment with subgroup, sensitivity and durability limitations.

levels.title: Serious harms and discontinuations
levels.objective: Characterize serious adverse events, deaths and discontinuations with correct denominators and context.
requirements: Reconcile adverse-event definitions, seriousness, causality, severity and discontinuation denominators.
Review deaths and withdrawals in both arms rather than relying on selected tolerability summaries.
completion_artifacts: Safety event/denominator assessment with causality and competing explanations.

levels.title: Organ toxicity and exposure safety
levels.objective: Assess organ-specific risks and adequacy of exposure for the proposed use.
requirements: Review laboratory, organ-specific and class risks, exposure duration and at-risk populations.
Identify limits of long-term or repeated-use safety and restrictions on exposure.
completion_artifacts: Exposure-adjusted safety and organ-risk assessment with missing long-term requirements.

levels.title: Benefit-risk and generalizability
levels.objective: Integrate benefit and harm for the intended clinical setting without converting gaps into a directional conclusion.
requirements: Compare benefits and harms at matched exposure and in the intended population.
Assess transferability to clinical practice, unmet need and uncertainty; missing evidence stays unknown.
completion_artifacts: Population-specific benefit-risk analysis with explicit uncertainties and competing interpretations.

levels.title: Consistency and independent reproducibility
levels.objective: Compare all relevant studies and reconcile registry, publications and sponsor disclosures.
requirements: Identify supportive and failed studies within the program and distinguish independent replication from reuse.

completion_artifacts: Cross-study reconciliation and independent verification record with unresolved conflicts.

levels.title: Regulatory pathway and interactions

levels.title: Manufacturing process and product quality

levels.title: Durability and follow-up-window audit
levels.objective: Evaluate persistence of benefit and whether follow-up supports the proposed treatment duration.
requirements: Reconcile time horizons, censoring, maintenance/extension populations and changes in treatment exposure.
Keep enriched withdrawal, open-label extensions and randomized comparisons distinct.
completion_artifacts: Time-specific benefit and follow-up limitations assessment.

levels.title: Serious adverse-event and discontinuation causality
levels.objective: Challenge safety summaries with complete arm-specific serious-event and discontinuation evidence.
requirements: Review event narratives, causality assessments, timing, denominators and comparator events, including deaths.
Distinguish all adverse events, treatment-related events and events causing discontinuation; do not compare incompatible fractions.
completion_artifacts: Independent safety-event/causality and discontinuation-denominator reconciliation.

levels.title: Exposure-adjusted and long-term safety
levels.objective: Assess whether exposure and follow-up can identify relevant delayed or repeated-use harms.
requirements: Review exposure duration, cumulative dosing and long-term follow-up by population and treatment.
Separate absence of observed harm from adequate power to exclude rare or delayed harm.
completion_artifacts: Exposure distribution and long-term/rare-harm uncertainty analysis.

levels.title: Organ, laboratory and class-risk investigation
levels.objective: Investigate organ-specific signals and biologically plausible class risks using complete supporting and contrary evidence.
requirements: Review clinically significant laboratory changes, organ events, dose relationships and competing causes.
Assess class effects and mechanistic plausibility without declaring causality from association alone.
completion_artifacts: Organ/class-risk evidence matrix with causality uncertainty and outstanding monitoring requirements.

levels.title: Dose, formulation and exposure bridging
levels.objective: Assess whether pharmacology and bridging justify extrapolation across doses, formulations or populations.
requirements: Review PK/PD, bioavailability, exposure-response and comparability evidence for the exact proposed formulation and population.
Identify where adult, prior-formulation or prior-pathway evidence does not establish efficacy or safety for the new use.
completion_artifacts: Source-bound dose/formulation/population bridging assessment and unresolved extrapolations.

levels.title: Successful and failed study reconciliation
levels.objective: Evaluate the entire development program without discarding unsuccessful studies.
requirements: Inventory positive, failed, inconclusive and terminated studies and explain design, exposure and analytic differences.
Distinguish within-program replication from independent external evidence and preserve unsuccessful primary endpoint labels.
completion_artifacts: Complete study-outcome and methodological consistency matrix.

levels.title: Registry, CSR and publication concordance
levels.objective: Resolve discrepancies across registry versions, full clinical reports, supplements and publications.
requirements: Compare populations, endpoints, dates, analyses, harms and disclosed amendments across original and corrected sources.
Record missing CSRs, supplements or registry versions; do not infer their content from a sponsor summary.
completion_artifacts: Cross-document concordance ledger, corrections and unresolved discrepancies.

levels.title: Independent numerical and audit-trail reproduction
levels.objective: Determine which principal findings can actually be independently reproduced from retained evidence.
requirements: Retain source bytes, calculations, software versions and reviewer decisions for independently reproduced analyses.
Separate verified arithmetic from inaccessible data, scientific interpretation and prediction-model validity.
completion_artifacts: Reproducible analysis package and limitations register with source/analysis identities.

levels.title: FDA review clock and action-event chronology
levels.objective: Distinguish final actions, target revisions and unresolved delays at the exact review-cycle horizon.
requirements: Verify original target, formal extensions, amendments, review cycle and final action with independent sources.
Do not label a missed target as an FDA extension without evidence; keep PASS, CRL, EXTENSION and unresolved events distinct.
completion_artifacts: Source-supported action/target-revision timeline with label horizon and unresolved dates.

levels.title: Pathway, designations and endpoint agreements
levels.objective: Evaluate actual regulatory implications of pathway choices, special designations and documented agreements.
requirements: Verify designation grant date and scope, pathway-specific evidence requirements and documented FDA endpoint feedback.
Do not treat priority review or other designations as approval, guaranteed timing or relaxed safety standards.
completion_artifacts: Dated regulatory pathway/designation/endpoint-agreement interpretation.

levels.title: Manufacturing change and batch comparability
levels.objective: Investigate process, scale and formulation changes against the product evaluated clinically.
requirements: Trace clinically studied and proposed commercial batches, process changes, comparability, validation and analytical controls.
Identify unsupported extrapolation across formulations, sites, scales or critical quality attributes.
completion_artifacts: Clinical-to-commercial manufacturing change and comparability matrix.

levels.title: Facility inspection and corrective-action closure
levels.objective: Determine whether inspection and quality-system concerns are resolved for the exact application and facility.
requirements: Review primary inspection/deficiency evidence, affected facilities, corrective actions and documented closure status.
Distinguish sponsor remediation claims, unrelated facility inspections and post-cutoff outcomes from contemporaneous verification.
completion_artifacts: Cutoff-bound facility/deficiency/corrective-action ledger and unresolved inspection risk.

levels.title: Stability, supply and vendor dependency stress test
levels.objective: Assess whether product quality and supply depend on unresolved stability, release or third-party constraints.
requirements: Review stability coverage, release specifications, supplier qualification and material/vendor dependencies.
Identify single-source, quality and supply continuity weaknesses without assuming a supply issue implies a specific FDA action.
completion_artifacts: Stability/release/supply dependency assessment with independently supported mitigations and unknowns.

levels.title: Historical comparator selection and causal limits
levels.objective: Prespecify historical clinical/FDA comparisons and examine mismatch or selection bias.
requirements: Match indication, population, comparator, endpoint, treatment era, pathway, review cycle and manufacturing context before inspecting candidate outcomes.
Keep program families and duplicate review cycles disjoint and do not treat historical cross-trial rates as causal head-to-head evidence.
completion_artifacts: Prespecified comparator inclusion/exclusion matrix, denominator proof and family/cycle deduplication record.

levels.title: Clinical setting and benefit-risk transfer
levels.objective: Evaluate whether the studied benefit-risk balance transfers to intended clinical use and current alternatives.
requirements: Assess real clinical use, competing treatments, unmet need and population/exposure differences.
Keep treatment-era and standard-of-care changes explicit; unavailable evidence remains unknown.
completion_artifacts: Intended-use and current-standard-of-care benefit-risk transfer assessment.

levels.title: Opposite-decision adversarial review
levels.objective: Construct and test the strongest clinical, statistical, safety, CMC and regulatory argument against the proposed decision.
requirements: Seek evidence supporting the opposite regulatory action and document contradictions, reviewer disagreement and alternative explanations.
State what evidence would change the conclusion and when the system must abstain.
completion_artifacts: Independent adversarial dossier and unresolved-disagreement/abstention record.

levels.title: Prospective evidence and prediction freeze
levels.objective: Create an auditable record before future outcomes become known rather than rebranding reconstructed historical forecasts.
requirements: Freeze exact application/cycle, prediction horizon, evidence cutoff, source features, model/training version and predictions with verifiable timestamps before the action.
Prespecify PASS/CRL/EXTENSION labels and abstention rules; retain revisions separately and never overwrite the original forecast.
completion_artifacts: Timestamped immutable evidence/model/prediction manifest and prespecified prospective evaluation protocol.

levels.title: Independent validation and uncertainty handoff
levels.objective: Evaluate unseen outcomes under the frozen protocol and distinguish scientific readiness from validated forecasting.
requirements: Verify independent outcome labels, chronology, complete denominators, program separation, calibration, discrimination, uncertainty and prediction/abstention coverage.
Report only measured performance; withhold unsupported three-class probabilities and preserve ABSTAIN when evidence or validation is inadequate.
Do not treat regression tests, completed task definitions or a favorable historical reconstruction as prediction accuracy or trading authorization.
completion_artifacts: Independent prospective validation report with model/prediction versions, uncertainty, exclusions and coverage; no trading authorization inferred.

levels.title: Opposite-decision adversarial review
levels.objective: Construct and test the strongest clinical, statistical, safety, CMC and regulatory argument against the proposed decision.
requirements: Seek evidence supporting the opposite regulatory action and document contradictions, reviewer disagreement and alternative explanations.
State what evidence would change the conclusion and when the system must abstain.
completion_artifacts: Independent adversarial dossier and unresolved-disagreement/abstention record.

levels.title: Prospective evidence and prediction freeze
levels.objective: Create an auditable record before future outcomes become known rather than rebranding reconstructed historical forecasts.
requirements: Freeze exact application/cycle, prediction horizon, evidence cutoff, source features, model/training version and predictions with verifiable timestamps before the action.
Prespecify PASS/CRL/EXTENSION labels and abstention rules; retain revisions separately and never overwrite the original forecast.
completion_artifacts: Timestamped immutable evidence/model/prediction manifest and prespecified prospective evaluation protocol.

levels.title: Independent validation and uncertainty handoff
levels.objective: Evaluate unseen outcomes under the frozen protocol and distinguish scientific readiness from validated forecasting.
requirements: Verify independent outcome labels, chronology, complete denominators, program separation, calibration, discrimination, uncertainty and prediction/abstention coverage.
Report only measured performance; withhold unsupported three-class probabilities and preserve ABSTAIN when evidence or validation is inadequate.
Do not treat regression tests, completed task definitions or a favorable historical reconstruction as prediction accuracy or trading authorization.
completion_artifacts: Independent prospective validation report with model/prediction versions, uncertainty, exclusions and coverage; no trading authorization inferred.

extended_investigation_framework.completion_rule: Definitions and source leads describe work; independent source-bound review and completion artifacts remain required.

contexts.name: Prior tradipitant gastroparesis submission
contexts.comparison: Same molecule, different indication and trials. Prior negative action is a source-specific challenge and family-overlap concern, not the motion-sickness outcome or an independent comparator.

requirements: Select comparator cases without using the candidate's later outcome.
Account for indication, endpoint, treatment era and review-cycle differences.
Verify complete sampling denominator and program-family independence before modeling.

supporting_context: A defined motion-sickness application/goal existed before the research cutoff; clinical efficacy and safety tables still require original-study reconstruction.
The December 4 issuer disclosure reports removal of the partial hold before the research cutoff; it supersedes the November 28 pending re-review status.
opposing_context: Gastroparesis results/CRL, motion-sickness partial-hold issues and later labeling/approval must remain separated by indication and publication date. Prior tradipitant staging raises a family-overlap check.
Hold removal concerned protocol exposure restrictions and acute event-driven use; it does not establish NDA approval, full efficacy or safety under other exposure patterns.
requirements: Review contrary efficacy, design, statistical, safety, regulatory and CMC evidence.
A missing document is unknown; it does not support either regulatory outcome.

missing_documents: Original protocols, amendments and prespecified SAP versions
Complete efficacy/safety tables and independent scientific review
Contemporaneous manufacturing/inspection evidence and exact availability

class_definitions.PASS: FDA approval for the exact application and review cycle at the prespecified review horizon.
class_definitions.CRL: An authenticated complete response letter for that review cycle; other unresolved or withdrawn actions are not CRLs.
class_definitions.EXTENSION: A documented formal FDA revision of the prespecified review target, distinct from a missed date, delay or later approval/CRL.
